name: Li Guangli's war against Dayuan
summary: To get the 'heavenly horses' of Ferghana, Emperor Wu sends an army 4,000 km west. The first campaign fails in the desert; the second, with 60,000 men, besieges the capital of Dayuan until its nobles kill their king and hand over the horses. Han power reaches the edge of Central Asia.

stops.note: Emperor Wu names Li Guangli 'Ershi general' after the city of Ershi, where the horses are kept.
The first army, starved by the oasis states, turns back.
A second army of 60,000 sets out.
After a 40-day siege the nobles kill their king and hand over 3,000 horses.

informs.note: The war of the Heavenly Horses against Dayuan
